scope: Read all four article pages and references; read full four-page motion BT20/10515 and debate physical59–62, including complete Rüffer speech. Visually checked debate physical60/printed21214. Opened official debate PDF independently. Welt page accessible only headline/standfirst, not full paid article.
assessment: The selective Rüffer fragment is followed immediately in the original speech by an explicit probability conditional on a positive result. Kappert-Gonther agrees with that conditional statement. Consequently, this primary source does not establish that either speaker confused false positives among positive results with false positives among all tests. However, the article labels the language as indicating a misinterpretation and later expressly gives its own judgment that the overall rate should not be called frequent or worrying. That can be read as interpretive criticism of risk communication rather than a categorical historical assertion about what the speakers understood. The quoted Welt statement might have a different scope; full surrounding article is unavailable.
alternative_explanations: The authors chiefly object to communication that omits the rarity of positive results, even if the speaker understands conditional probability. This is an evaluative disagreement, not a proven factual error.
The newspaper passage may be the main target; no full-text claim about its actual qualifications can be made.
Authors explicitly welcome monitoring and ask that it use current facts; they do not oppose the entire motion.
limits: No new diagnostic-accuracy finding. Clinical calculation correctness is not independently re-adjudicated here; nothing in this review establishes the actual motivations, comprehension or intent of the speakers or authors.
provenance_note: Committee receipt is after the9October hearing. Do not infer the article was supplied before or orally delivered at that hearing.
quotation_note: No additional verbatim submission quotations added.
